subject: Re: Private / VPC pricing follow-up — PaymentsAI
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood Private / VPC pricing

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups we promised to surface: 

- Summary: PaymentsAI is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to host inference for fraud-model serving and customer support generation. Primary needs: dedicated VPC deployment, KMS integration, and support for ~3 environments (dev/stage/prod).
- Questions we still need from your side to finalize a pricing run: token volumes (monthly) for inference traffic, target unit economics (e.g., target $/1M tokens), expected concurrency/throughput, and whether you want a term/discounted licensing commit or pay-as-you-go.
- Redwood ask: for Private/VPC we typically model pricing as a combination of a base platform license (annually) + reserved GPU capacity (monthly/annual commit) + support tier. Examples attached (Redwood_Private_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf).

Concrete next steps:
1) If you can share a budget range and rough monthly token volumes (low/expected/high), we can produce a couple of pricing scenarios (payg vs reserved + license).
2) Confirm environment count (dev/stage/prod + DR?) and whether separate VPCs are required per environment.
3) If procurement wants it, we can provide a statement-of-work draft and term sheet for review (attached SOW draft).

Target timelines: If we get volumes and budget this week, we can get back with a tailored pricing + recommended config by Friday.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf, PaymentsAI_SOW_Draft.docx

From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@paymentsai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@paymentsai.com, Lisa Chung <lisa.chung@paymentsai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood Private / VPC pricing

Ben — thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers from our side: 

- Token volumes (monthly): 
  - Low: 50M tokens
  - Expected: 400M tokens
  - High: 1.2B tokens (seasonal spikes / batch jobs)
- Budget range (annual): aiming for $150k–$400k for the platform + infra licensing in year 1 (open to committed vs. consumption tradeoffs).
- Target unit economics: we'd like to be in the ~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens range (our procurement/finance will push hard on unit cost).
- Environments: dev + stage + prod, plus a hot-standby DR region — so effectively 4 environments. Ideally a single VPC with isolated subnets, but we can do separate VPCs if that's easier for billing/segmentation.
- Support: interested in a 24x7 standard support tier with a named technical contact; willing to consider premium support if SLA and response times justify the uplift.

Procurement wants an initial pricing worksheet + SOW to move the internal approval. Can you produce both with a couple of variants (payg, 1-yr commit, 3-yr commit)?

Best,
Alex Soto
Head of Infrastructure
PaymentsAI
alex.soto@paymentsai.com
+1 (617) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@paymentsai.com>, procurement@paymentsai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood Private / VPC pricing

Alex — perfect, thanks for the details. A few clarifying items so we model the right config: 

1) When you say "1.2B tokens high" — is that primarily inference (per-token generation) or embedding/indexing workloads? Embeddings change the economics (batch vs online).
2) Concurrency: for prod peak concurrency, are you targeting 200 qps of short responses (avg 80 tokens) or more batch-oriented throughput?
3) DR: for the hot-standby, do you want active-active (dual-region, both serving) or active-passive (failover)? This affects reserved capacity sizing.

Partnering note: based on the token ranges and target unit economics you quoted, initial back-of-envelope shows we should be able to get into the $1k per 1M token range with a 1yr reserved commit + platform license and careful batching / KV caching. We'll produce payg / 1yr / 3yr model outputs showing unit $/1M tokens, license fees, and recommended environment sizing.

I'll have a draft pricing worksheet and SOW variants by EOD Friday. Marissa — please prepare two configs to run numbers on: (A) payg + basic license, (B) 1yr reserved + standard support + license.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing model inputs — prepping scenarios

Ben — forwarding internal notes. Draft assumptions I'm using for the two configs: 

- Workload breakdown: 80% inference generation (avg 120 tokens per request), 20% embeddings (batch).
- Monthly token mix (expected): 400M tokens generation, 50M tokens embeddings converted to equivalent tokens for cost modeling.
- Environment sizing: dev (1 GPU, on-demand), stage (2 GPUs reserved small), prod (6 GPUs reserved), DR (2 GPUs warm standby).
- License: annual platform license modeled as $60k (payg) or $45k (1yr commit) or $30k/year (3yr commit).
- Support uplift: standard 10% of license, premium 25% of license.

I tagged the pricing sheet (internal tab) with these assumptions — will adjust if Ben/Alex confirm different splits.

-Marissa

Thanks Ben/Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what procurement asked for. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Embeddings will be batch (1x nightly job) and can be priced separately — treat as 20% with batch discounts if possible.
- Concurrency for prod is expected to peak ~150 qps of short responses (~80 tokens).
- DR: active-passive failover is fine for now — we don't need active-active.

Please send the 3 pricing variants (payg, 1yr commit, 3yr commit) and the SOW draft. Procurement would like a line-item export (CSV) for their FP&A template if possible.

We'll aim to review by next Tuesday and schedule a procurement + engineering sync if the numbers look reasonable.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Alex
